ActivateSubscription.name: ActivateSubscription
ActivateSubscription.documentation: Activates a Subscription to enable billing for a user.

CreateDataset.name: CreateDataset
CreateDataset.documentation:
Creates a Dataset in a Domain and starts building it. A new dataset has the status CREATING. When it's ready to use, its status changes to ACTIVE, or to CREATE_FAILED if it fails to build. To check the status, call GetDataset.

This operation is idempotent: if you retry a request with the same clientToken, it returns the dataset that the first request created.

For a medical coding dataset, Amazon Connect Health uses the coded examples that are in the s3InputPath when you create the dataset, and writes evaluation scores to the s3OutputPath. Later changes to the s3InputPath don't change the dataset. To use this operation, you must have s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket permissions for the input location and s3:PutObject permission for the output location, and kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey permissions if you encrypt the locations with an AWS KMS key.

Datasets are in preview release and are subject to change.

CreateDomain.name: CreateDomain
CreateDomain.documentation: Creates a new Domain for managing HealthAgent resources.

CreateSubscription.name: CreateSubscription
CreateSubscription.documentation: Creates a new Subscription within a Domain for billing and user management.

DeactivateSubscription.name: DeactivateSubscription
DeactivateSubscription.documentation: Deactivates a Subscription to stop billing for a user.

DeleteDataset.name: DeleteDataset
DeleteDataset.documentation:
Starts deleting a Dataset and the resources that Amazon Connect Health built for it. You can delete a dataset whose status is ACTIVE, CREATE_FAILED, or DELETE_FAILED. The dataset moves to DELETING, and then to DELETED. If the delete fails, the dataset moves to DELETE_FAILED, and you can call DeleteDataset again.

Medical coding jobs that already use the dataset finish. Amazon Connect Health rejects new requests that specify the dataset.

Datasets are in preview release and are subject to change.

DeleteDomain.name: DeleteDomain
DeleteDomain.documentation: Deletes a Domain and all associated resources.

GetDataset.name: GetDataset
GetDataset.documentation:
Retrieves information about a Dataset, including its status and, after it is built, its results. A dataset whose status is DELETED returns ResourceNotFoundException.

Datasets are in preview release and are subject to change.

GetMedicalCodingJob.name: GetMedicalCodingJob
GetMedicalCodingJob.documentation:
Retrieves information about a medical coding job, including its status and, when it succeeds, the location of its results.

Medical coding jobs are in preview release and are subject to change.

GetMedicalScribeListeningSession.name: GetMedicalScribeListeningSession
GetMedicalScribeListeningSession.documentation: Retrieves details about an existing Medical Scribe listening session

GetPatientInsightsJob.name: GetPatientInsightsJob
GetPatientInsightsJob.documentation: Get details of a started patient insights job.

ListDatasets.name: ListDatasets
ListDatasets.documentation:
Lists the Datasets in a Domain. You can list only the datasets of one type. The operation doesn't return datasets whose status is DELETED, and the order of the results isn't specified. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.

Datasets are in preview release and are subject to change.

ListTagsForResource.name: ListTagsForResource
ListTagsForResource.documentation: Lists the tags associated with the specified resource

StartMedicalCodingJob.name: StartMedicalCodingJob
StartMedicalCodingJob.documentation:
Starts an asynchronous job that generates medical codes (ICD-10 and CPT) for clinical text. Call GetMedicalCodingJob to check the status of the job. When the job succeeds, Amazon Connect Health writes the results to the output Amazon S3 location.

To tailor the codes to your organization, specify an ACTIVE medical coding dataset in the Domain. If you don't specify a dataset, the job uses the general medical coding knowledge base.

Medical coding jobs are in preview release and are subject to change.

StartMedicalScribeListeningSession.name: StartMedicalScribeListeningSession
StartMedicalScribeListeningSession.documentation: Starts a new Medical Scribe listening session for real-time audio transcription

SubmitFeedback.name: SubmitFeedback
SubmitFeedback.documentation: Submits feedback on a clinical document or a set of medical codes that Amazon Connect Health generated.

TagResource.name: TagResource
TagResource.documentation: Associates the specified tags with the specified resource

UntagResource.name: UntagResource
UntagResource.documentation: Removes the specified tags from the specified resource

reason.documentation:
The reason for review. The following values are valid:

  • SITE_NOT_CHARTED: One or more sites have no reading.

  • VALUE_NOT_CHARTED: A dictated value or charting instruction was not charted, for example because the value was out of range or not valid at its position.

  • READING_COUNT_MISMATCH: The number of dictated values did not match the number of open sites. The values were charted as dictated.

  • LINE_UNCLEAR: A line of dictation could not be interpreted and was not charted.

  • TOOTH_UNCLEAR: A line of dictation did not identify the tooth and was not charted.

  • MISSING_TOOTH_CONFLICT: The dictation conflicts with a tooth marked as missing.

  • MEASUREMENT_NOT_CHARTED: The dictation included a measurement that the chart does not record, such as plaque, calculus, or the mucogingival junction.

  • SESSION_ISSUE: The exam setup could not be used and all teeth were assumed to be present, or the earlier chart could not be restored and charting restarted.

documentation:
Amazon Connect Health is an AI-powered healthcare service built on Amazon Connect. It provides pre-built agents that automate patient engagement workflows and support clinical documentation at the point of care.

You can use the Amazon Connect Health API to programmatically manage domains, configure patient engagement agents, run patient insights jobs, and stream ambient documentation sessions. This API reference describes the available API operations and data types for Amazon Connect Health.

We recommend that you use the AWS SDKs to make programmatic API calls to Amazon Connect Health.
